Jeremiah

Introduction

Prophet Hirimiyas, began his work as a prophet at the year of 627 before Kristu was born and continued until around the year of 580 before Kristu was born. During the long time of serving by Hirimiyas, he warned people concerning the destruction that will_come to the nation due to their sins, and their worshiping the false_gods. And Hirimiyas was_able_to_see the fulfillment of his prophesy when Hirusalim was ruled_under Nibukadnisar the king of Babilunya. He also saw the destruction of the city and the temple, and capturing many people with their kings to Babilunya. He prophesied also (about) the returning of the people from their capturing, and the rebuilding of the nation to its former position.

The Reading_Document by Hirimiyas was divided into five: 1/ The calling of Hirimiyas; 2/ what_ God (MS Manama) _has_spoken for the nation of Huda and its leaders during the kinging by Husiyas, Huwakim, Hihuyakin and Sidikiyas; 3/ everything that people had experienced according to what was written by Baruk the secretary of Hirimiyas, including the different (kinds) of prophesy, and the important (things) which happened to Hirimiyas' life; 4/ what_ the Lord God _said concerning the foreigners there in the nations; and 5/ other stories concerning the destruction of Hirusalim, and the capturing of the people to Babilunya.

Hirimiyas was a passionate person; he greatly loved his people, and he disliked (those) who condemns/judges them. There are parts of the reading_document that (shows) his great love to share/tell about his sufferings because he was called by God to be_a_prophet. The word of the Lord is like a fire in his heart, and he can't hide it.

It is also written here in this document that the time will_come that there will be a new agreement. And that agreement will_be_cared and obeyed by the people of God, even if no teachers who reminds them because it will_be_written in their hearts. (31:31-34)

Sirayas was an official of the king. 60 I wrote_down to the scroll writing_document all destruction that will_happen to Babilunya, everything indeed concerning Babilunya. 61 And I said to Sirayas, “When you(sg) arrive in Babilunya, read aloud to the people everything that is written here in this reading_document. 62 Then, pray(sg) saying, ‘O Lord God, you(sg) said that you(sg) are_going to destroy this place so_that no more animals and people who can_live here. And this will_turn into a desert because it can't be_lived_in by the people without ending.’ 63 [xr]And when you(sg) finish reading, bind it to a stone and throw it to the River of Iyupratis 64 and say, ‘This is what will_happen to Babilunya. It will_sink and it never come_out due to destruction that the Lord God will_make_ them _to_experience.’ ”

And Hirimiyas' story ends here.

The destruction of Hirusalim

(2 Kings 24:18–25:7)

521 Sidikiyas was twenty one (21) years old when he became king, and he kinged there in Hirusalim for eleven (11) years. Hamutal the child of Hirimiyas from_Libna was his mother. 2 And Sidikiyas also did evil to the Lord God, like all what King Huwakim did. 3 Therefore the Lord God was very angry with the people of Hirusalim and Huda, and he drove_ them _away.

Then Sidikiyas rebelled (against) Nibukadnisar the king of Babilunya.4 [xr]Therefore on the tenth day of the tenth month on the ninth year of Sidikiyas' kinging, Nibukadnisar king of Babilunya invaded/attacked Hirusalim. They camped outside the city, then they sieged the soil around the high and thick stone fence/wall of Hirusalim so_that they can enter. 5 They surrounded the city until the eleventh (11) year of kinging by Sidikiyas. 6 And then, nobody could bring food into the city, so the people were experienced a famine. On the ninth day of the fourth month on that (same) year, there was no food left at all in the city. 7 [xr]Then the ones from Babilunya broke down part of the high and thick stone fence/wall of the city. Therefore Sidikiyas fled with all his soldiers on the night time even the city was surrounded by the (ones) from_Babilunya. They passed_through the planting_place/garden of the king near the gate which was the boundary of the two wall of the city which is high and thick stones, and they went to the valley of Hurdan. 8 But they were chased by the soldiers of Babilunya, and they were caught in the plains of Hiriku. Then King Sidikiyas was abandoned by his soldiers who were scattered. 9 Then they captured King Sidikiyas and they took him to King Nibukadnisar there in the city of Ribla which_was_under_jurisdiction of the nation of Hamat. And there, he was judged/sentenced by King Nibukadnisar. 10 And Nibukadnisar had the male children of Sidikiyas killed there in front of him, including all the officials of Huda. 11 [xr]Then Nibukadnisar had_ the eye(s) of Sidikiyas _taken_out. Then he was_bound with a chain and took (him) there to Babilunya. And he imprisoned Sidikiyas there until he died.

(2 Kings 25:8‑17)

12 On the tenth (10) day of the fifth month of the nineteenth (19) year of kinging by Nibukadnisar in Babilunya, Nibusaradan the leader of the guard of the king in Babilunya was_able_to_enter Hirusalim. 13 [xr]Then he burned the temple of the Lord God, the palace of the king, including all the houses in Hirusalim, and the houses of the well_known people in Hirusalim. 14 Then his soldiers tore_down the high and thick stone fence/walls of the city. 15 And Nibusaradan captured the people who were left in the city, including the poor people, and the soldiers who surrendered to the soldiers of the king of Babilunya, including those skilled workers. 16 But he left_behind the rest of the very poor people, so that they (are) the (one) to take_care of the vineyards and fields.

(2 Kings 25:18‑21, 27‑30)

24 And also Nibusaradan captured Sirayas the High Sacrificer, Supuniyas the entrusted/assistant of Sirayas, and the three officials in the temple. 25 And he also arrested the official of the soldiers, and the seven advisors of the king, and the secretary of the officers who was in_charge_of_listing people to be the soldiers, and sixty (60) other people found in the city of Hirusalim. 26 And Nibusaradan took_ them all _with_him to the king of Babilunya there in Ribla. 27 And the king of Babilunya caused_ them _to_be_beaten and killed.
